questions.question: 12 spherical balls of radius 10 cm are dropped in a bucket that is full of water up to the brim. The water that flowed out is collected in a cylindrical jar of radius 20 cm. What is the height (in cm) of water in the jar? (Take pi = frac{{22}}{7} )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of balls = 12

Radius of spherical balls (r) = 10 cm

Radius of Cylindrical Jar (R) = 20 cm

Height of cylinder = h

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Sphere = (4 × π × r³ )/(3)

Volume of Cylinder = π × R² × h

**Concept:**

Volume of water displaced = volume of objects submerged

Water takes the shape of the object in which it is placed (Here it is taken in cylindrical jar)

∴ Volume of cylinder = Volume of Sphere.

**Calculation:**

According to question,

Volume of cylinder =12 × Volume of Sphere

⇒ π × R2 × h = 12 × (4 × π × r³ )/(3)

⇒ h = 40 cm.

**∴ The height (in cm) of water in the jar is 40 cm.**

questions.question: The sum of two numbers m and n is 84 (m > n) and their difference is 6. What is the ratio of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
Given:

Sum of two numbers m and n = 84

Difference is 6 

Calculation:

m + n = 84 ----(1)

m - n = 6 ----(2)

On adding equation (1) and (2), We get

m + n + m - n = 84 + 6

⇒ 2m = 90 

⇒ m = 45

By putting the value of m in equation (1)

⇒ n = 39

According to question,

Ratio of the two numbers = 45/39

⇒ m/n = 15/13

**∴ The ratio of the two numbers is 15/13.**

questions.question: P sold a lamp to Q at a profit of 20%. Later, Q sold the lamp to P at a profit of 30%, thereby making a profit of ₹108. How much (in ₹) did P pay originally for the lamp?
questions.solution:
Given:

P sold a lamp to Q at a profit of 20%

Q sold the lamp to P at a profit of 30% , making a profit of ₹108

Formula Used:

Selling Price = Cost Price × (100 + P)%

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article for P be ‘x’.

P sells it to Q at a profit of 20%.

⇒ Selling price of P = x × (100 +20)%

⇒ 1.2x

Selling price for P = Cost price for Q

Q had a profit of 30%.

Selling Price for Q = 1.2x × (100 + 30)%

⇒ 1.2x × (130/100)

⇒ 1.56x

According to question,

Q makes a profit of ₹108

⇒ 1.56x - 1.2x = 108

⇒ 0.36x = 108

⇒ x = 108/0.36

⇒ (108/36) × 100

⇒ 300

**∴ P pay originally for the lamp (in ₹) 300.**

Here for "Q" CP is 60 units and SP is 78 units

Then, the profit of "Q" is 18 unit 

18 units are equal to 108

50 units is equal to (108 ÷ 18) × 50 = 300

questions.question: Seema is younger than Reema by 8 years. If 4 years back, their ages were in the ratio 1 : 2, then the age (in years) of Seema after 6 years from now will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

Seema is younger than Reema by 8 years

Ratio of ages four years back = 1 : 2

Calculation:

Let Reema = R and Seema = S

According to the question,

R - S = 8 ----(1)

Four years back, 

Reema's age = (R - 4)

Seema's age= (S - 4)

Ratio of their ages = (S - 4)/(R - 4)

⇒ (S - 4)/(R - 4) = 1/2

⇒ 2S - R = 4 ----(2)

By solving equations (1) and (2),

⇒ S = 12 years

Now Seema's age after 6 years = 12 + 6 = 18 years

**∴ The age (in years) of Seema after 6 years from now will be 18.**

According to the question

⇒ (2a + 4) - (a + 4) = 8

⇒ 2a + 4 - a + 4 = 8

⇒ a = 8

Seem present age = 8 + 4 = 12

**∴ The age of Seema after 6 years = 12 + 6 = 18 years**

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/h. The time taken by the boat to go 35 km downstream is 1.25 times the time taken by it to go 14 km upstream. How much time (in hours) will it take to go 60 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The speed of a boat in still water (X) is 10 km/h.

Time taken by the boat to go 35 km downstream is 1.25 times the time taken by it to go 14 km upstream

Distance upstream = 35 km

Distance downstream = 14 km

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed Upstream = Speed of a boat in still water (X) - Speed of the current (Y) km/h

Speed Downstream = Speed of a boat in still water (X) + Speed of the current (Y) km/h

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

(35)/((10 + Y)) = 1.25 × (14)/(10 - Y)

⇒ (5)/((10 + Y)) = 1.25 × (2)/(10 - Y)

⇒ (10 - Y) = .25 × 2 × (10 + Y)

⇒ (10 - Y) = .50 × (10 + Y)

⇒ (10 - Y) = 5 + .5Y

⇒ 1.5Y = 5

Y = 10/3 km/h.

Now, Speed downstream = 10 + 10/3 = 40/3 km/h

Time taken for 60 km downstream = (60)/(40/3)

⇒ 9/2

⇒ 4.5 h

**∴ The time (in hours) it will take to go 60 km downstream is 4.5**.

questions.question: The least number of square tiles required to pave the floor of a room with dimensions 15 meters and 12 meters will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

Length of Room = 15 meters

Breadth of room = 12 meters

Concept used:

To find the least number of square tiles we have to find the highest common factor of Length and Breadth

Calculation:

Length of room = 15 meters

Breadth of room = 12 meters

So, H.C.F of 15 and 12 

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 12 = 3 × 2²

Here, only 3 is common

So, H.C.F = 3

Now, Area of 1 tile = 3 × 3

Area of Room = 15 × 12

Number of tiles required = (15 × 12) / (3× 3)

⇒ Number of tiles required = 20

∴ Number of tiles required is 20.

questions.question: The average weight of 24 persons in a group is 72 kg. If 3 persons with average weight 78 kg leave the group and 4 persons of average weight 75 kg join the group, then what will be the average weight (in kg) of the persons in the group now?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average weight of 24 persons in a group is 72 kg

3 persons with average weight 78 kg leave and 4 persons of average weight 75 kg join the group

Formula Used:

Average = (Sum of the observations/Number of observations)

Calculation:

According to question,

Average weight = 72 kg

Number of persons = 24

Sum of total weight = 72 × 24 

⇒ Sum of total weight = 1728 Kg

Now Sum of total weight of persons who left = 78 × 3

⇒ 234 Kg

Now Sum of total weight of persons who join = 75 × 4

⇒ 300 Kg

Total weight of the persons present in the group = (1728 + 300 - 234) Kg

⇒ 1794 Kg

Number of persons present in the group = 24 + 4 - 3

⇒ 25

Average = Total weight/Number of persons 

⇒ Average = 1794/25

⇒ 71.76 Kg

**∴ The average weight (in kg) of the persons in the group now is 71.76 Kg.**

questions.question: The average weight of 56 students in a group is 55 kg. If 12 students of average weight 60 kg leave and 6 students of average weight 52.5 kg join the group, then the average weight of the remaining students in the group decreased by:
questions.solution:
Given:

Average weight of 56 students in a group is 55 kg

12 students of average weight 60 kg leave and 6 students of average weight 52.5 kg join the group

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of weights/Number of students

Calculations:

Average weight of class = 55 kg

Number of students = 56

Total weight of the class = 55 × 56

⇒ 3080 Kg

Average Weight of 12 old students leaving the group = 60 Kg

Total weight of 12 students = 12 × 60

⇒ 720 Kg

Average Weight of 6 new students joining the group = 52.5 kg

Total weight of 6 new students joining the group = 52.5 × 6

⇒ 315 Kg

Total weight of the class now = 3080 - 720 + 315

⇒ 2675 Kg

Number of student left in the class = (56 - 12 + 6)

⇒ 50

New average weight = 2675/50 = 53.5 Kg

Average weight is decreased = (55 - 53.5) Kg

⇒ 1.5 Kg

**∴ The average weight of the remaining students in the group decreased by 1.5 Kg.**

questions.question: The speed of train is 110 km/h. It is increased by 20% and then runs at uniform speed. The train driver sees the 'Slow Down' sign, So he reduces the speed of train by 40% of the speed at that moment. What is the final speed(in km/h, correct to one decimal place) of the train?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of train = 110 km/h.

Formula Used:

Successive Speed formula,

If speed is increased by X% and decreased by Y% then, 

Resultant speed = [X - Y - (X × Y)/100]%

Calculation:

According to question,

Speed of train = 110 km/h.

⇒ X = 20% and Y = 40%

⇒ Resultant Speed = 20 - 40 - (40 × 20)/100 (By formula above)

⇒ Resultant Speed = - 28% (here -ve sign shows that Speed is decreased by 28%)

⇒ Resultant Speed = (100 - 28)% 

⇒ Final Speed = 72% of original speed.

⇒ 72% × 110 km/h

⇒ 79.2 km/h

∴ The final speed(in km/h) of the train is 79.2. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Given:

Speed of train = 110 km/h.

Concept:

If X is increased by 10 % then we calculate (100 + 10)% of X

and If X is decreased by 10 % then we calculate (100 - 10)% of X.

Calculation:

According to the question,

Speed of train = 110 km/h.

Now it is increased by 20%

⇒ New speed of train = 110 × 120% km/h.

⇒ 132 km/h

Now, Speed reduces by 40%

⇒ Final speed of train = 132 × 60% km/h.

⇒ 79.2 km/h

**∴ The final speed(in km/h) of the train is 79.2.**
